_comment: SAT-SA negative-space rule configuration.
NEGATIVE SPACE IS NOT 'A FIELD IS MISSING'
Negative space is: evidence that is expected in a DEFINED CONTEXT is
absent. So a rule here is only valid when it can state four things:
1. the expectation          -- what evidence should exist
2. the trigger population   -- which records make it expected
3. the observable concept   -- how the evidence is observed
4. why it is expected       -- the supervisory reasoning
A canonical field being empty is not on its own a weakness. Nothing in
this file fires because a field is blank; every rule must first prove
that its trigger population exists.
HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM AN EXECUTION GAP
execution gap     CRITICAL present AND escalation explicitly says
NOT_ESCALATED  -> a control was contradicted
negative space    CRITICAL population exists AND no usable escalation
evidence was submitted -> evidence is absent
The two never overlap. This layer counts the PRESENCE of evidence and is
indifferent to its value; the execution-gap layer judges the VALUE. A
record with an explicit NOT_ESCALATED has evidence, so it can raise an
execution gap but never a negative-space signal.
NO POLICY THRESHOLDS
'material_coverage_threshold' is null everywhere in this file, and that
is deliberate. A configured threshold would be a supervisory policy
decision about what proportion of missing evidence is tolerable, and
SAT-SA must not invent one. Complete absence and partial absence are
reported as different, factual states; how much attention either
deserves is a later prioritisation phase.
Same canonical form as the execution-gap rules: trimmed, upper-cased,
separators folded to underscores. Reusing one normalisation keeps
the two layers from disagreeing about what a value means.
framework/tests/test_negative_space.py asserts the two rule
configurations agree on the escalation tokens.
The values that constitute a submitted escalation OUTCOME, i.e.
evidence that a determination was recorded rather than left open.
A populated value outside this set is reported separately as
unusable evidence instead of being silently counted as present.
A blank, N/A or absent cell is not evidence at all.
The trigger tokens are declared for the same reason the
escalation tokens are: mappings.json defines no allowed_values for
any concept, so the supervisory vocabulary is declared explicitly
here rather than guessed at detection time. N/A and PENDING are
absent from BOTH sets on purpose. A token that could also mean 'not
applicable' or 'not yet determined' proves neither that a
determination was made nor that it was declined, so it establishes
no expectation outcome in either layer.

rules.name: Critical alert activity expects escalation evidence
description: An assessment scope containing critical alert activity is
expected to carry escalation evidence for that same population.
This is a supervisory expectation, not an observed fact.

expectation.statement: When a scope contains critical alert activity, escalation evidence is expected for those alerts.
why_expected: A critical severity assessment implies a supervisory
escalation decision is warranted, so a record of that
decision is expected to exist for the population the tool has

_comment: Deliberately null. There is no configured policy threshold
that turns partial coverage into a failure, because choosing
one would be SAT-SA inventing a supervisory policy. The
mechanism is honoured if a supervisory authority later
supplies a number; until then partial coverage is reported as
an observation.

rationale: SECURITY_SEVERITY and ESCALATION_STATUS both exist in

unavailable_rules.name: Alert activity expects investigation evidence
missing_evidence: No canonical concept expresses the relationship between an alert
and the investigation it should have generated.
investigation_context.notes maps to INVESTIGATION_EVIDENCE, but
there is no case or investigation identifier, and no field
recording whether an investigation was required.
SECURITY_SEVERITY alone cannot establish the expectation: not
every alert warrants an investigation, so a scope of low and
medium alerts would produce a false positive.

population would convert an unestablished expectation into a
finding. The expectation itself is unsupported, not merely the
would_require: A canonical concept recording investigation expectation, such as

unavailable_rules.name: Critical systems expect telemetry
missing_evidence: asset_context.criticality is a canonical field with no concept in
mappings.json, so no source column can populate it.
monitoring_context.telemetry_available and coverage_status are
likewise canonical fields with no concepts.
No monitoring source inventory exists.
why_not_implemented: There is no way to establish which systems are critical, so the
trigger population for this rule cannot be formed.
would_require: Mapping concepts for asset criticality and monitoring telemetry,

unavailable_rules.name: Expected alert categories are present
missing_evidence: THREAT_CATEGORY maps to alert_context.category, but no expected
alert taxonomy exists anywhere in the repository.
mappings.json declares no allowed_values for the concept.
why_not_implemented: Without a taxonomy supplied by a supervisory authority, 'the
expected categories' is undefined. Any list would be SAT-SA's
would_require: A configured expected-alert taxonomy per Critical Sector Entity.

unavailable_rules.name: Activity is not unexpectedly low
missing_evidence: No historical baseline, no expected record volume, and no
peer group exists.
why_not_implemented: Low activity is only meaningful relative to an expectation. With
no baseline of any kind, every period looks low or high and no
would_require: A historical or peer baseline of expected record volume.

unavailable_rules.name: No monitoring blind spots
missing_evidence: Same as critical_systems_expect_telemetry: no concept for asset
criticality and no monitoring inventory or coverage status.
why_not_implemented: A blind spot is a gap between expected and actual monitoring
coverage. Neither side of that comparison is observable.
would_require: Monitoring coverage concepts and an inventory of monitored assets.

unavailable_rules.name: No peer-relative absence of evidence
missing_evidence: No peer group definition, no comparable-entity baseline, and no
benchmark data in the canonical model.
why_not_implemented: Peer benchmarking is explicitly out of scope for this phase and
would additionally require a defensible peer cohort.
would_require: A peer cohort definition and comparable-entity evidence,
